title: Irregular preterites: ser, ir, hacer, tener, estar…
summary: The most common verbs change their stem in the preterite: fui, hice, tuve, estuve, pude, puse, vine, dije, di, vi.
focus: Irregular preterite stems and their unstressed endings
content:
## Ser and ir: the same forms

In the preterite **ser** (to be) and **ir** (to go) are identical. Context tells you which one it is, and none of the forms carries an accent:

| person | ser / ir |
|---|---|
| yo | **fui** |
| tú | **fuiste** |
| él / ella / usted | **fue** |
| nosotros/as | **fuimos** |
| vosotros/as | **fuisteis** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **fueron** |

- *Fui a Grecia el año pasado.*: I went to Greece last year. (ir)
- *Mi abuelo fue médico.*: My grandfather was a doctor. (ser)
- *Fuimos al cine anoche.*: We went to the cinema last night. (ir)

## Strong stems, soft endings

A group of very common verbs swaps its stem for a **strong stem** and takes its own set of endings: **-e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron**. The stress stays on the stem, so **yo** and **él/ella** have **no accent**: *tuve*, *tuvo* (compare regular *comí*, *comió*).

| person | tener → tuv- |
|---|---|
| yo | tuv**e** |
| tú | tuv**iste** |
| él / ella / usted | tuv**o** |
| nosotros/as | tuv**imos** |
| vosotros/as | tuv**isteis** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | tuv**ieron** |

- *Tuve un examen ayer.*: I had an exam yesterday.
- *Ana tuvo que trabajar.*: Ana had to work.

## The seven stems to memorise

| verb | stem | yo | él / ella |
|---|---|---|---|
| hacer | **hic-** | hice | **hizo** |
| tener | **tuv-** | tuve | tuvo |
| estar | **estuv-** | estuve | estuvo |
| poder | **pud-** | pude | pudo |
| poner | **pus-** | puse | puso |
| venir | **vin-** | vine | vino |
| decir | **dij-** | dije | dijo |

Two spelling details:

- **hizo** has a **z** because the **c** becomes **z** before **o** to keep the soft sound (*hice, hiciste, hizo*).
- **dijeron**, not *dijieron*. After a stem ending in **j**, the **i** of **-ieron** is dropped. The same happens with *trajeron* (traer).

- *¿Qué hiciste el fin de semana?*: What did you do at the weekend?
- *No pude dormir.*: I couldn't sleep.
- *Ellos dijeron la verdad.*: They told the truth.

## Dar and ver: short and accent-free

**Dar** and **ver** take the regular **-er/-ir** endings, but the forms are so short that the **yo** and **él/ella** forms are written **without** an accent:

| person | dar | ver |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **di** | **vi** |
| tú | diste | viste |
| él / ella / usted | **dio** | **vio** |
| nosotros/as | dimos | vimos |
| vosotros/as | disteis | visteis |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | dieron | vieron |

- *Mi madre me dio un regalo.*: My mother gave me a present.
- *¿Viste la película?*: Did you see the film?

vocabulary.example: El año pasado fuimos a Grecia.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Last year we went to Greece.
What did you do at the weekend?

vocabulary.example: Tuvieron un examen la semana pasada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: They had an exam last week.

vocabulary.example: Puse el regalo en la mesa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I put the present on the table.

vocabulary.example: Mi madre me dio un regalo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My mother gave me a present.
Did you see the film last night?
We took a trip to Lisbon.

vocabulary.example: Me dio un regalo muy bonito.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She gave me a very nice present.

quiz.prompt: El año pasado nosotros ___ a Grecia.
quiz.explanation: Ir in the preterite: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. 'Fuimos a Grecia' = we went to Greece.
hints: Ser and ir share the forms fui, fuiste, fue…

quiz.prompt: ¿___ (tú, hacer) el viaje a Lisboa al final?
quiz.explanation: Hacer takes the strong stem hic-: hice, hiciste, hizo… 'Hiciste' = you did/made.

quiz.prompt: Mi abuelo ___ médico durante cuarenta años.
quiz.explanation: Ser in the preterite uses the same forms as ir. Mi abuelo = él, so 'fue'. No accent.

quiz.prompt: La semana pasada mis hermanos ___ (tener) un examen.

quiz.explanation: Poder → pud- plus the unstressed yo ending -e: 'pude'. 'Pudo' is he/she, 'puedo' is present.
hints: Strong stems take -e for yo, no accent.

quiz.prompt: ¿Dónde ___ (vosotros, estar) ayer? No vinisteis a clase.

quiz.explanation: Decir → dij-, and after the j the i of -ieron is dropped: 'dijeron'.

quiz.prompt: Mi madre me ___ (dar) un regalo y lo puse en la mesa.
quiz.explanation: Dar: di, diste, dio… 'Dio' is one syllable, so no accent. 'Puse' is poner → pus-.
hints: One syllable, so no written accent.

quiz.explanation: Ver: vi, viste, vio, vimos, visteis, vieron. Tú = 'viste'; 'vio' never takes an accent.

listening.text: Mis padres me dieron un regalo.
listening.meaning: My parents gave me a present.
listening.note: Dar: di, diste, dio, dimos, disteis, dieron, no accents.

listening.meaning: What did you do yesterday afternoon?

listening.text: Anoche fui al teatro con Luis.
listening.meaning: Last night I went to the theatre with Luis.
listening.note: New word: el teatro = the theatre.

listening.meaning: Where did you all put Marta's present?

listening.text: Mi abuela fue profesora en un pueblo.
listening.meaning: My grandmother was a teacher in a village.
listening.note: New word: el pueblo = the village, the town.

listening.text: Carlos no dijo la verdad sobre el viaje.
listening.meaning: Carlos didn't tell the truth about the trip.

listening.text: No pude venir a la fiesta porque tuve mucho trabajo.
listening.meaning: I couldn't come to the party because I had a lot of work.
listening.note: Strong stems pud- and tuv-: no accent on pude, tuve.

listening.text: El año pasado hicimos un viaje a Italia y vimos muchas cosas bonitas.
listening.meaning: Last year we took a trip to Italy and saw many beautiful things.

guide.tip: Say them as a chant: hice, tuve, estuve, pude, puse, vine, dije. Stress on the stem, never on the ending.

conversations.title: The birthday party
conversations.scenario: Diego missed Sofía's birthday party. The next day he asks her how it went.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Hola, Sofía! Lo siento, ayer no pude ir a tu fiesta.
lines.meaning: Hi, Sofía! I'm sorry, yesterday I couldn't come to your party.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: No problem. What did you do?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tuve que trabajar hasta las nueve y después estuve en el hospital con mi abuela.
lines.meaning: I had to work until nine and afterwards I was at the hospital with my grandmother.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Oh no! And how is she?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Mejor, gracias. Bueno, cuéntame: ¿quién vino a la fiesta?
lines.meaning: Better, thanks. Anyway, tell me: who came to the party?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vinieron casi todos. Marta y Luis fueron los primeros en llegar.
lines.meaning: Almost everyone came. Marta and Luis were the first to arrive.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: And what did they give you?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Mis padres me dieron un libro y mi hermana me dio un regalo enorme: ¡una bicicleta!
lines.meaning: My parents gave me a book and my sister gave me a huge present: a bicycle!

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Great! Where did you put it?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: La puse en el garaje. Al final fuimos todos al parque y vimos las estrellas.
lines.meaning: I put it in the garage. In the end we all went to the park and watched the stars.
lines.note: poner: puse · ir: fuimos · ver: vimos

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Todos me dijeron que fue una fiesta genial. ¡El año que viene no me la pierdo!
lines.meaning: Everyone told me it was a great party. Next year I'm not missing it!

bites.title: Ser = ir in the past
bites.rule: Fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron work for both ser and ir. Context decides: fui médico (was) and fui a Madrid (went). No accents.
bites.example: Fuimos a Grecia y fue un viaje genial.
bites.example_meaning: We went to Greece and it was a great trip.

bites.title: Strong stem, soft ending
bites.rule: hic-, tuv-, estuv-, pud-, pus-, vin-, dij- + -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. The stress sits on the stem, so tuve and tuvo have no accent.
bites.example: Tuve un examen y no pude dormir.
bites.example_meaning: I had an exam and I couldn't sleep.

bites.title: hizo and dijeron
bites.rule: Hacer writes hizo (c → z before o). Decir drops the i after j: dijeron, never dijieron.
bites.example: Ella hizo la cena y ellos dijeron gracias.
bites.example_meaning: She made dinner and they said thank you.

bites.title: di, dio, vi, vio
bites.rule: Dar and ver use regular -er/-ir endings but are so short that yo and él/ella get no accent: di, dio, vi, vio.
bites.example: Mi madre me dio un regalo.
bites.example_meaning: My mother gave me a present.

sorts.title: Ser or ir?
sorts.why: The forms are identical. A destination (a + place) means ir, a description or identity means ser.

sorts.title: Which stem?
sorts.why: hacer → hic-, tener → tuv-, poner → pus-, decir → dij-.

sorts.title: Accent or no accent?
sorts.why: Regular preterites stress the ending (comió, salí). Strong stems, ser/ir, dar and ver carry no written accent.

spots.sentence: Ayer yo hací la cena para toda la familia.
spots.why: Hacer uses the strong stem hic- and the unstressed ending -e: hice.
After the j of dij- the i is dropped: dijeron.

spots.sentence: Mi madre me dió un regalo.
spots.why: Dio is one syllable and never takes an accent.
Strong stems take -e for yo, with no accent: pude.

spots.sentence: El año pasado nosotros fuemos a Grecia.
spots.why: Ir in the preterite: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron.
Hacer uses the strong stem hic-: hiciste. There is no form haciste.
